answer: For an atlas poll about a relic on a knoll, the server checks for a separate $10 escrow bound to each ballot key; it rejects missing or reused escrows. Officials randomly audit accepted ballots, asking selected voters to sign a challenge with their ballot key in person. They refund audited voters who pass and forfeit the escrows of those who fail; unaudited escrows are refunded. Each extra ballot ties up $10 and risks forfeiture. Recruits can attend, and distant voters face a burden.
